findings.title: Google Calendar stores the Zod safeParse wrapper as the credential key
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole Zod safeParse result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credential object. The code assigns that wrapper to `data.key` when updating the credential. On the next refresh/use, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` receives `{ success: true, data: ... }` instead of the credential and fails. Store `key.data` after checking success instead.

findings.title: Sharing mode returns a fetch Response where callers expect token data
findings.body: When credential sharing is enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` Response. Callers expect provider-specific token data: Google does `res?.data` (undefined), Hubspot writes the Response object into the credential and reads `accessToken`/`expiresIn` off it, and Zoho does `tokenInfo.data.error` on a Response. This makes sync fail or store corrupt credentials. The function also never checks `response.ok`, so an error response can be treated as success. Return one consistent parsed-token contract and update all callers.

findings.title: Minimum token schema does not allow the fields it is meant to accept
findings.body: `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is built with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]`; both computed properties resolve to the same string and the second overwrites the first, so this is not a catchall. Zod therefore strips every response field except `access_token`, including `refresh_token`, `expires_in`/`expiry_date`, and `instance_url`. The next `if` then sets `refresh_token` to the literal string `'refresh_token'` whenever it was stripped. In sharing mode this drops expiry/refresh/instance fields and writes a fake refresh token, corrupting credentials and breaking later refreshes.

findings.title: Schema choice is based on env, not on whether the sync endpoint was used
findings.body: The parser switches to the minimal sharing schema solely because env vars are set. However `refreshOAuthTokens` falls back to the provider when `userId` is null, and Salesforce always refreshes directly. Those provider responses are still parsed with the minimal schema even though no sync endpoint was involved, stripping required fields such as `instance_url`, `expiry_date`, and scope. The helper should receive a flag indicating the response source, or the caller should choose the schema.

findings.title: Salesforce service uses prisma without importing it
findings.body: `prisma.credential.update` is called here, but this file never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. This is a TypeScript/build error for the Salesforce app. Add the import or remove the DB write.

findings.title: Salesforce bypasses the new sync helper and ignores the refreshed token
findings.body: The new refresh code posts directly to `login.salesforce.com` instead of calling `refreshOAuthTokens`, so `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is never used for Salesforce and the self-hosted app store cannot be the source of truth. Additionally, after updating the DB with the freshly refreshed token, the returned jsforce connection is still built with the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url`, so the refreshed token is not used for the current connection.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends credential id as calcomUserId
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens`' third argument is the Cal.com user id and is sent in the request body as `calcomUserId`, but this call passes `credentialId`. The self-hosted endpoint receives a credential id where it expects a user id, so it cannot identify the user whose credentials should be refreshed. Pass `credential.userId` instead.

findings.title: Zoom sync request uses the wrong app slug
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens` sends `appSlug` to the credential sync endpoint. Zoom's app slug is `zoom` (the callback creates credentials with `appId: 'zoom'`), but this call sends `zoomvideo` (the folder name). The self-hosted endpoint will not find or sync the correct app. Use `zoom`.

findings.title: Updated credentials do not clear the invalid flag
findings.body: On the update path only `key` is written. If the existing credential was previously marked `invalid: true` (for example after an `invalid_grant`), it remains invalid after the app store sends fresh credentials, so the synced token is still ignored by the app. Set `invalid: false` (and any other required fields) when applying fresh credentials.

findings.title: Find-then-create is not atomic and can create duplicate credentials
findings.body: `findFirst` followed by `create` is not atomic. Two webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both see no credential and then both create rows, producing duplicate credentials. Later updates only touch the first row via `findFirst`, leaving the other stale. Use a unique constraint plus upsert/transaction, or otherwise serialize this path.

findings.title: New credential sync webhook and refresh paths have no tests
findings.body: This PR adds an authenticated webhook that writes credentials and changes token refresh behavior across many integrations, but no tests cover missing/invalid secret, malformed encrypted payload, update vs create, invalid-flag recovery, fallback when the sync endpoint is absent, or provider-specific response parsing. These paths are high risk and currently unverified.
